content:
"We are getting leads, but they don't convert." It is one of the most common complaints from business owners, and Gurugram is no exception. A B2B supplier in Udyog Vihar may get enquiries from students and job seekers. A clinic on Golf Course Road may get form fills from people who never pick up the phone. An IT services firm in Cyber City may get plenty of cheap leads from ads, yet close almost none of them.

The cause is usually the same. Somebody was asked to produce leads, so they optimised for the number of forms submitted. Our lead generation services in Gurugram start from the other end: what does a lead worth calling look like for your business, and what has to happen between the ad click and the sales call for that person to become a customer?

First, we agree what a "lead" means

Before any campaign is built, we sit down with you and whoever handles sales, and write a one-page definition. It covers:

  • Who qualifies: location, company size or household profile, budget range, and timeline.
  • Who doesn't: the enquiries you want filtered out, such as job applications, vendors pitching to you, or requests for services you don't offer.
  • What a sale is worth to you, roughly, so we know how much you can sensibly pay per qualified lead.
  • What happens next: who calls, how quickly, and how the outcome is recorded.

This takes about an hour and it changes everything that follows. Campaign targeting, form questions and reports are all built around it.

Picking channels by how your buyers decide

B2B and high-value services

Buyers research, compare and involve colleagues. Google Search campaigns on problem and service searches, LinkedIn campaigns aimed at job titles and industries, and a website with proper service pages and detailed content usually work well. Lead volume is lower; each lead is worth more. Long forms are acceptable here because they filter out casual enquiries.

Local consumer services

Clinics, salons, coaching centres, interior designers and home services depend on people nearby searching when they need something. A well-maintained Google Business Profile, local search campaigns targeted to specific sectors and localities, and click-to-call or click-to-WhatsApp ads fit this pattern. Speed of response matters more than anything else.

Considered consumer purchases

Education, property, cars and similar decisions take weeks. Meta and Google lead forms help build a pipeline, but follow-up by WhatsApp, SMS and email over several weeks does most of the converting.

What we build

  1. Tracking. Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager, ad platform conversion tags and call tracking are set up so every lead can be traced to its source. Without this, no one can tell which spend is working.
  2. Landing pages. One page per offer, loading quickly on mobile, with a form that asks the questions from your lead definition. Sending ad traffic to a general homepage wastes money.
  3. Campaigns. Search, social or LinkedIn campaigns, depending on the channel plan above, with negative keywords and audience exclusions to keep out the people you don't want.
  4. Lead forms with filters. For Meta and Google lead forms, we add qualifying questions and, where it helps, use the higher-intent form option that asks people to review their details before submitting.
  5. Instant routing. Leads go straight to your CRM, or to a shared sheet and an email or WhatsApp alert if you don't use a CRM yet, with an automatic acknowledgement to the enquirer.
  6. Feedback loop. Your team marks each lead's outcome. We feed qualified leads and sales back into the ad platforms where possible, so their algorithms learn to find more people like your real customers.

The first 90 days

Weeks 1–3: lead definition, tracking audit and setup, landing pages, and campaign build. Weeks 4–8: campaigns go live on a controlled budget. We check search terms and lead quality every few days, cut what brings junk and shift budget to what brings qualified enquiries. Weeks 9–12: with a few weeks of sales outcomes recorded, we can see real cost per qualified lead and cost per sale by channel, and decide with you whether to scale, change or stop each channel.

We are honest about the early weeks. The first month is partly spent learning, and results rarely peak straight away.

Numbers we report

  • Total leads
  • Qualified lead rate
  • Cost per lead
  • Cost per qualified lead
  • Response time
  • Lead-to-meeting rate
  • Cost per sale

We treat cost per lead on its own as a misleading figure. A channel with double the cost per lead can be the cheaper one if its leads close three times as often.

Why leads fail after they arrive

  • Slow response. A lead called the next day has often already spoken to two competitors.
  • No record of outcomes. If sales doesn't mark results, campaigns can't be improved beyond form counts.
  • One call and done. Many people don't answer the first call from an unknown number. A planned sequence of calls and messages over a few days recovers many of them.
  • Form too easy. A one-tap form brings volume, not intent.
  • Offer too vague. "Contact us for more details" gives nobody a reason to act.

What you need to bring

An ad budget that you are comfortable testing with for at least two to three months, access to your website and ad accounts (owned by your business, not us), someone who will follow up leads the same day, and a willingness to share honest sales outcomes. We handle the rest.

Who should not hire us for this

If you want a fixed number of leads guaranteed at a fixed price, we are the wrong agency. Anyone promising that is usually either buying data or counting junk. Lead generation is also a poor fit if you have no capacity to follow up, if your offer is not yet clear, or if your business depends on one or two very large contracts a year that come through personal networks rather than search or social.

Questions business owners ask us

Do you sell databases or ready lead lists?

No. We generate enquiries from people who have actively responded to your ads, website or profile. Purchased lists produce poor results and raise consent and privacy problems.

Which is better for leads: Google or Facebook?

It depends on whether people search for what you sell. If they do, Google Search usually brings higher intent. If they don't yet know they need it, Meta can create demand. Many Gurugram businesses use both, with different jobs for each.

How much should we spend on ads?

It depends on your market, the competition for your keywords, and what a customer is worth to you. We suggest a starting budget after the consultation and adjust it once we see real cost per qualified lead. Our management fee is separate and quoted as a fixed amount after a free consultation.

Can you connect leads to our existing CRM?

In most cases yes. Common CRMs can receive leads from Meta, Google, LinkedIn and website forms, either directly or through an integration tool. If you don't have a CRM, we can set up a simple one or a shared sheet to begin with.

We are in Gurgaon but sell across India. Does that matter?

Not at all. Campaigns can target any region. Being local simply means it is easy to meet in person and sit with your sales team when needed.
